analysis.title: They just keep buying
key_insights: The dollar is rallying even as US tech stocks have sold off sharply, which is the opposite of what the author argued would happen.
The market has repriced a more hawkish Fed after recent commentary, which widened the interest rate differential, but the dollar appears to be overshooting that move (figure 1).

Foreigners have been aggressive buyers of US equities during the selloff. The author's tracker of more than 100 foreign-domiciled ETFs shows the largest dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners so far this year, over the last two weeks.
The author doubts that both the wider rate differential and the aggressive foreign equity buying can continue if market turmoil persists, and will monitor foreign investor behaviour in coming weeks.

sector_views.rationale: US tech stocks have sold off sharply. The note gives no sector rating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Repricing of a more hawkish Fed has widened the differential, but the dollar is overshooting this move. The author doubts the widening can continue if market turmoil persists.

risk_factors: Continued market turmoil could end both the widening in interest rate differentials and the foreign buying of US equities.
vol_and_positioning: Foreign-domiciled ETF flows into US equities over the last two weeks are the largest dip-buying spree so far this year, per the author's tracker of more than 100 ETFs.

key_data_points.context: The tracker shows the largest foreign buying of US stocks so far this year over the last two weeks.

tension_points.bull_case: A more hawkish Fed has widened the interest rate differential, and foreigners are buying US equities on the dip, which supports the dollar.
tension_points.bear_case: The dollar looks to be overshooting the rate move, and neither the wider differential nor the foreign dip-buying can continue if market turmoil persists.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Persistent market turmoil, which the author says would end both the rate differential widening and the foreign equity buying.

theme_stances.key_argument: The author doubts the wider rate differentials and the aggressive equity buying can continue if market turmoil persists.
theme_stances.evidence: we are doubtful both the widening in interest rate differentials
